transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Leo Ramirez (Redwood SE), Avery Park (Redwood Ops), Jordan Blake (Arkadia - Procurement), Priya Singh (Arkadia - CISO), Omar Reyes (Arkadia - Lead SRE), Sanaa Malik (Arkadia - Legal)

Summary:
Quick procurement review covering MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiers, pricing for hosted vs dedicated, and onboarding timeline. Customer asked about encryption/KMS, audit logs retention, data residency, and fallback/availability guarantees. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send redlines and pricing options, schedule security deep-dive, and provision trial for benchmarks.

Topics:
- MSA/DPA redlines
- SLA tiers and uptime/latency targets
- Pricing and dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs
- Security: KMS, SOC2, audit logs, data residency
- Onboarding and benchmarking plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, with Leo our SE and Avery from ops. Uh, Jordan, Priya, Omar, Sanaa, thanks for making time.
[00:22] Jordan: Sure, thanks. Quick note, we've got about an hour, Priya needs to jump to another meeting around 15:45 UTC but should be here for the key bits.
[00:30] Maya: Okay great, we'll try to be efficient. The goal for today is to walk the MSA/DPA redline items you sent, cover SLA options and pricing tradeoffs, and confirm next steps for onboarding.
[00:45] Priya: That sounds right. Our security team flagged KMS integration, audit logs retention, and data residency as must-haves. Also we need clarity on how Redwood manages keys in Dedicated vs Hosted.
[01:05] Leo: Yep, good question. For Hosted we do customer-specific KMS via external key wrapping — let me, uh, explain how that works. In Dedicated, customers have the option to use their own KMS in VPC mode; the private control plane can integrate with HSM-backed KMS. There was a note in the docs about key rotation windows, which we can make more explicit.
[01:30] Omar: Sorry to interrupt, do you have specifics on network egress controls? We can't have model traffic going through public internet for some flows.
[01:41] Leo: Right, for Private/Dedicated we support VPC peering and private networking. There are, uh, a couple of patterns — private control plane with data plane in-customer VPC, or full on-prem (air-gapped) install in extreme cases. We'll share the topology doc.
[02:02] Sanaa: On the DPA, legal redlined section 5.3 around subprocessors. We're trying to limit subprocessors and get notification windows.
[02:12] Maya: Totally. We saw those redlines. We can accept a 30-day notice for new subprocessors and a list of current subprocessors. We typically commit to notifying customers and offering mitigation.
[02:25] Jordan: For procurement timing, we need pricing options with monthly committed spend, and then a PO process. Can you give us a matrix for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[02:36] Avery: Yes, we'll send a pricing spreadsheet. High level: Hosted is usage-based with per-token/embedding rates, Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits and lower unit costs for sustained throughput. We'll include an example for your 1k qps-burst profile.
[02:55] Priya: SLA details — we need 99.9% uptime floor for the production route, and latency SLOs in 99th percentile under typical load. Do you have different SLA tiers?
[03:10] Leo: We offer three SLA tiers for enterprise: Standard (99.5), Business (99.9), and Premium (99.95) with different support and SLOs. For latency we provide per-route latency dashboards and tracing; Premium includes proactive alerts and a runbook for failover. For cost-sensitive workloads we also provide model-fallback policies — automatically route to a cheaper variant if capacity is constrained.
[03:40] Omar: Does the automatic fallback maintain the same model semantics? We're worried about quality regressions if a fallback triggers.
[03:49] Leo: Good point. Fallbacks are to compatible model variants with a quality degradation profile, and we have feature flags to control fallbacks per-route. We'll also provide evaluation runs we did — model quality delta numbers — so you know the tradeoff.
[04:10] Jordan: On liability caps in the MSA — our legal is pushing for higher caps for critical services. Are you open to negotiating?
[04:18] Maya: We can discuss commercial terms. Typically liability caps are tied to contract value and SLA tier. We'll pass your ask to pricing/legal and include options in the redline we send.
[04:30] Priya: We also need SOC 2 and ISO attestations and an audit log retention option up to 7 years for compliance audits.
[04:40] Maya: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications; audit logs are available with configurable retention — we'll confirm retention tiering and export formats.
[04:55] Sanaa: A couple of DPA clauses — data residency and deletion: How fast can you delete PII on request?
[05:05] Leo: We have a data deletion workflow; for Hosted it depends on GC cycles but we guarantee deletion within X days — I'll check the exact SLA and put it in writing. In Dedicated/Private it's customer-controlled.
[05:20] Jordan: Can we talk about onboarding timeline? If procurement signs in September, we want production by November. Is that realistic?
[05:30] Avery: Yes, that's feasible. Typical onboarding for Dedicated is 6-8 weeks from signed SOW for reserved capacity, Hosted can be faster. We need a 2-week benchmark window to validate latency/throughput on your workload.
[05:45] Omar: For the benchmark, we need to run with our auth and routing. Can you support a VPN tunnel or staging VPC?
[05:54] Leo: Yes, we can spin a staging VPC and support private peering; for Hosted we'll provide a secure trial account with VPC peering options where necessary. We'll document the steps.
[06:10] Jordan: Pricing — we need committed monthly numbers and an overage policy. Also any onboarding fees?
[06:20] Avery: We'll include a sample committed pricing table with overage rates and an optional onboarding professional services line item. For Dedicated there is usually an initial capacity reservation fee.
[06:33] Priya: Do you support customer-managed keys in Hosted? You mentioned external key wrapping earlier — can you be explicit about where plaintext lives and what encryption-at-rest guarantees are?
[06:45] Leo: Sure. In Hosted, we encrypt at rest, and you can supply a customer KMS key via external key wrapping. Plaintext is only in-memory on the inference node; we use ephemeral instance memory and rotate caches — though I should note that some internal caches may be persisted depending on config, we'll provide config options and default to minimal persistence.
[07:10] Priya: Okay, please send that in writing. We need it for our security questionnaire.
[07:15] Maya: Will do. We'll attach the architecture note and the KMS section.
[07:22] Jordan: Regarding subprocessors, is there a list of cloud providers and observability vendors you use? We need that to run our vendor risk assessment.
[07:34] Maya: Yes, current subprocessors include AWS, GCP for backups in some regions, Datadog for monitoring, and a couple of CDN providers. We'll send an up-to-date list and commit to advance notice on changes.
[07:50] Sanaa: On indemnity, we asked for clearer language around data breaches caused by Redwood negligence. Can legal follow up?
[07:59] Maya: Yes, I'll loop in our legal contact after this call.
[08:05] Jordan: One more thing on SLAs — credits vs termination remedies. We want credits for repeated monthly misses and an exit right if severity is continuous.
[08:15] Maya: That's something we can provide in an enterprise SOW for premium tiers. We'll propose a credit schedule and an escalation path.
[08:25] Priya: Also, logging format — we need structured logs for security telemetry (JSON). Can logs be exported to our SIEM?
[08:33] Leo: Yes, JSON structured logs are supported and we can push to your SIEM via secure collector or S3 export. We'll include sample log schema.
[08:48] Omar: For the production deployment, we'll need CPU/GPU sizing guidance. Our predicted sustained throughput is around 250 tokens/second averaged per route but bursts to 1k qps for a minute or two.
[09:02] Leo: For that profile, Dedicated with autoscaling and burst capacity is recommended. We'll run capacity planning and provide the estimated GPU types and counts — note that tokenization and sequence length vary the compute; we'll ask for representative prompts.
[09:18] Jordan: How do you handle quantization and model variants? We want to know if quantized models are supported in Dedicated.
[09:26] Leo: Yes, quantization-friendly execution paths are supported; we have recommendations per model. For some model families we run 8-bit or 4-bit quantization with little quality loss; we'll include model/quantization recommendations.
[09:44] Maya: To recap next steps: we'll send MSA + DPA with proposed SLA tiers and liability options, pricing spreadsheet with Hosted vs Dedicated examples, and architecture/KMS/auth docs. Also schedule the security deep-dive and provision a trial for a 2-week benchmark.
[10:05] Jordan: Sounds good. Can you target EOD Thursday for the docs?
[10:10] Maya: Yes — we'll aim for 2026-08-13 EOD.
[10:15] Priya: After we get the docs we'll schedule the security deep-dive; Omar and I will be present.
[10:20] Sanaa: Legal will review redlines and get back with counterpoints.
[10:24] Maya: Great. Anything else?
[10:28] Omar: One small ask — can you include a simple runbook for incident response and emergency contacts?
[10:33] Avery: Absolutely, we'll include runbook and escalation contacts in the SOW appendix.
[10:38] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll expect the package and confirm procurement timeline.
[10:43] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up via email and log next steps in the CRM.
[10:48] Priya: Thanks.
[10:50] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, small speaker attribution inconsistencies). Shared artifacts referenced: link to MSA/DPA redline (internal), pricing spreadsheet (to be sent), architecture doc and KMS note (to be sent).
